bib.title: MIND2WEB: Towards a Generalist Agent for the Web
bib.venue: NeurIPS 2023 Track on Datasets and Benchmarks

read.skipped: Reference list skimmed only (lineage); figure images not viewed

question: How can we build and evaluate a generalist agent that follows language instructions to complete tasks on any real-world website?
hypothesis: Filtering raw HTML with a small LM before an LLM predicts the action makes LLMs effective on real websites, including unseen websites and domains.
contributions: MIND2WEB, the first dataset for generalist web agents: over 2,000 tasks, 137 websites, 31 domains, real-world websites with crowdsourced action sequences
MINDACT, a two-stage small-LM ranker plus LLM multi-choice action predictor
Initial exploration of LLMs on the dataset, with three generalization levels (Cross-Task, Cross-Website, Cross-Domain)

method.summary: Crowdsourced (MTurk) demonstrations on real websites with cached snapshots; MindAct fine-tunes DeBERTa-v3-base to rank DOM elements (top-50), then Flan-T5 (fine-tuned) or GPT-3.5/GPT-4 (3-shot) pick the element via multi-choice QA in groups of five plus None and generate the operation. Evaluation is offline, each step scored independently with ground-truth history.
method.task: web navigation / element grounding and action prediction from HTML

datasets.name: Mind2Web
datasets.size: 2,350 tasks (of 2,411 collected), 137 websites, 31 domains, 5 top-level domains, avg 7.3 actions, avg 1,135 elements per page
datasets.split: Train 1,009 tasks from 73 websites; Test Cross-Task 252 tasks from 69 websites (random 20% of remaining data); Test Cross-Website 177 tasks (10 websites from each remaining top-level domain); Test Cross-Domain 912 tasks from 73 websites (Information and Service held out)
datasets.source: MTurk annotators (>=1,000 approved HITs, >98% approval), Playwright tool; websites chosen by similarweb US popularity; train data CC BY 4.0, code MIT
datasets.preprocessing: Heuristics keep visible, semantically meaningful elements: avg elements 1,135 -> 580, target recall 94.7% in training data. Click/Hover/Press Enter mapped to Click. Equivalent-element heuristic (nearest clickable ancestor plus visible descendants in bounding box) makes all such elements positive in training and evaluation.

models.name: Flan-T5 base/large/XL (action predictor)
models.params: 220M (base); large and XL sizes not stated in text

training.objective: Ranker: binary cross entropy on sigmoid matching score, target element positive and randomly sampled negatives. Predictor: left-to-right LM objective on target sequence (choice letter, action, value)
training.hardware: flan-t5-xl and flan-t5-large: 4*A100 80GB (Ohio Supercomputer Center); all other models: single A6000 48GB
training.seeds: 5 random seeds only for the option-grouping analysis (Table 5); main table seed count not stated

other.negatives_sampling: random negatives from the page, count not stated

inference.samples: one run per item for the main results; Table 5 averages 5 seeds of random grouping
inference.prompting: GPT models: system message plus 3 demonstrations in multi-choice format (Table 8); task, previous actions, options A None of the above, B..., answer then Action and Value
inference.retrieval: DeBERTa top-50 candidates for all models except GPT-4 which uses top-10; candidates split into groups of five; if several options are chosen, new groups of the selected ones are formed until one remains or all groups choose None

metrics.name: Element Accuracy
metrics.definition: selected element compared with all acceptable elements

metrics.name: Operation F1
metrics.definition: token-level F1 of predicted operation (with value for Type and Select Option); equals accuracy for Click

metrics.name: Step Success Rate
metrics.definition: step succeeds only if both element and operation are correct; macro average across tasks

metrics.name: Success Rate
metrics.definition: task succeeds only if all steps succeed

metrics.name: Recall@50
metrics.definition: target element within top-50 ranked candidates

baselines: Flan-T5B direct generation of target element
eval.protocol: Offline cached snapshots; each step evaluated independently with ground-truth action history; GPT-4 run on 50 tasks per split only (budget); no confidence intervals in Table 2; 5-seed std only in Table 5

availability.data: https://huggingface.co/datasets/osunlp/Mind2Web (CC BY 4.0); test data on a password-protected link

prompts.purpose: ChatGPT seed task generation for annotators
prompts.text: We are testing the website ... We want to test practical daily tasks that a user would do on the website. Come up with a list of 5 example tasks and try to cover different cases. Requirements: - Each example should be a single sentence and not just click one of the elements. - Don't give step-by-step instructions or directly mention the element to interact. - Describe the goal of the task and provide concrete information or constraints. Use mock-up information (identifier, number, personal information, name, date, attributes, constraints, etc.) to make the task more specific and realistic.
You are a helpful assistant that is great at website design, navigation, and executing tasks for the user

prompts.purpose: GPT action prediction user turn template
prompts.text: Based on the HTML webpage above, try to complete the following task: Task: ... Previous actions: ... What should be the next action? Please select from the following choices (If the correct action is not in the page above, please select A. 'None of the above'): A. None of the above B. ...

limits: Open-loop offline evaluation: each step is scored with ground-truth history, and a valid path not cached during collection fails, giving false negatives (authors concede)
Mostly English US websites; MTurk annotators may be biased toward proficient web users
Pages encoded independently each step; no modelling of interaction dynamics
Single-turn task goal; no human-agent interaction
GPT-4 only evaluated on 50 tasks per split, top-10 candidates, so not comparable to full-test Flan-T5 numbers (Table 7 shows subset numbers lower)
Task SR from stepwise independent scoring does not reflect compounding of errors in live execution
No confidence intervals on main table; weights and sizes of large/XL not given in text
Live end-to-end evaluation is left to future work
